scope: 21 requested named species/taxon candidates plus one unresolved bat-order record; 19 other bird species, legacy cabaret redpoll and white shark. Companion native-species research is outside this file.
status: design research only; no sample assets or production registration

method.availability_definition: Public source page and listed media/player references verified in page metadata; no promise of successful playback, permanent hosting or reusable sample rights
method.proposal_definition: All numeric synth controls, musical register/envelope/timbre and synthesis-family assignments are original hypotheses. They are not transcriptions, natural-frequency estimates or owner approvals.
method.archive_date_caution: Raw published dates are identifiers for finding references, not independently established observation precision.
coverage_limits: Most sources are New Zealand archive examples; this is not a global dialect survey.
No complete species repertoire is claimed; selected contexts prioritize contrast.
Published descriptors cannot replace direct listening and level-matched musical evaluation.
Scientific names and provider ids are preserved separately from later taxonomic treatments.

control_units_and_ranges.scope: Current controls provide a rough starting contour only; proposed extensions are not implemented or approved. Gain proposals anticipate ensemble balancing, not calibrated natural loudness.

rights.policy_summary: Public personal/reference listening is distinct from redistribution. Commercial reproduction and unauthorized metadata mining are restricted. No recorded audio is copied into the project. Selected links are research references; do not turn them into a sample pack or automatic bulk collector.

species.musical_hypothesis: Use a compact, woody, slightly nasal keyboard chip: two unequal pulses, tiny upward scoops and dry silence between clusters. Flock density becomes restrained overlap, not a continuous glitter wash.
species.musical_gesture: upper-mid; clipped attack; mildly rough harmonic body; uneven two/three-note cells; fast release
species.relationship_and_distinction: Keep shorter and drier than goldfinch; no long greenfinch buzz. Sparrow-like appearance of dunnock is not a family relationship.

species.acoustic_coverage: Song-versus-fast-alarm phrasing is documented. A clean flute-like synthesis is a design hypothesis; no Hz limits or attack/decay measurements were established here.

species.musical_hypothesis: Design a projecting high reed/brass voice with a nasal rising middle and a sliding fall, in spaced repeated cries. The chick option uses much smaller, softer points and remains separately labelled.
species.musical_gesture: upper-mid; definite onset; bright nasal harmonics; long bent cry with spaced repeats; sliding taper
species.relationship_and_distinction: Phasianidae sibling of pheasant. Distinguish with a stretched cry and open spectral band, not merely higher output level.

species.taxon_scope: legacy exact named taxon; IOC now places it within Acanthis flammea
species.evidence_basis: Primary recordist publication and descriptions; no listening or signal measurement
species.documented_observations: Primary recordists describe compact fast flight-call groups, commonly two or three units, sometimes interspersed with an upward-inflected social call. Two named cabaret examples cover flight alone and flight plus social context.
species.acoustic_coverage: Rhythm and rising social contour are described. Exact frequency range, durations and tonal/noisy proportions remain unmeasured. No generic common-redpoll recording is silently substituted.

species.musical_hypothesis: Use a light dry reed/pizzicato voice in pairs and triplets, interrupted occasionally by one upward sigh. The rise is a deliberately musical analogue of the described social contour.
species.musical_gesture: high; small fast onset; dry fine harmonic grain; two/three-note packets and occasional rising answer; short release
species.relationship_and_distinction: Finch-family relation to goldfinch/greenfinch/chaffinch; maintain dry small packets rather than fluid goldfinch rolls or greenfinch sustained buzz.

species.evidence_basis: Primary shark-sound paper plus government species/telemetry research; absence of exact-species evidence in this review is not proof of silence
species.documented_observations: No established Carcharodon carcharias vocal repertoire or exact-species call recording was found. A 2025 first-shark-sound study concerns juvenile Mustelus lenticulatus under handling, not Carcharodon. DOC/NIWA describe seasonal long-distance movements and coastal/offshore habitat use for white sharks.
species.acoustic_coverage: No supported vocal rhythm, register, spectrum, envelope or phrasing. All proposed acoustic dimensions are artistic invention, not reconstructed shark calls.

species.musical_hypothesis: Explicit nonvocal metaphor: a low warm bowed/rounded tone with a slow descending spectral opening and long space, suggesting large-scale travel. Any pulse is compositional, never labelled as a heartbeat, fin beat, sonar or shark call. A location report can trigger this sound without inventing a continuous track.
species.musical_gesture: low; slow swelling onset; dark harmonic body; one long arc separated by silence; long release
needed_extensions: sustain and release beyond struck-note envelope
species.relationship_and_distinction: Shares slow musical contour machinery with goose/dove only by design. Do not transfer calls from rig, rays, whales or imagined underwater ambience.

unresolved_records.reason: Chiroptera is an order containing many species, not an exact species identification. No species-specific echolocation contour, ultrasonic band or audible voice can be assigned from this record.
unresolved_records.mapping_policy: Retain unresolved order provenance. Request/use a genuine species-level detection before researching an exact-species voice; a generic order fallback must be explicitly labelled and separately approved.

perceptual_design_research.status: primary literature reviewed; hypotheses not listening-validated

references.authors: McAdams, Winsberg, Donnadieu, De Soete and Krimphoff
references.title: Perceptual scaling of synthesized musical timbres: Common dimensions, specificities, and latent subject classes
references.evidence: Ratings of synthetic instrument timbres were modelled with common dimensions, sound-specific attributes and listener classes. Attack rise, spectral centre and spectral change helped explain the common dimensions; listeners weighted cues differently.
references.design_inference: Use related starting bodies plus distinctive temporal/spectral gestures, with owner evaluation. A fixed brightness-only taxonomy or a fixed small palette cannot be justified by this study.
references.limit: Instrument stimuli and perceptual ratings do not establish animal taxonomy, natural vocal structure or a complete synthesis parameter set.

references.title: Acoustic correlates of timbre space dimensions: a confirmatory study using synthetic tones
references.evidence: Controlled synthetic-tone experiments supported attack time, spectral centre and spectrum fine structure as perceptually useful dimensions. Spectral flux was less consistently salient and depended on how many other dimensions varied.
references.design_inference: Make attack shape, spectral envelope and harmonic distribution independently controllable; audition spectral motion against competing changes instead of assuming it always creates an obvious identity.
references.limit: This is evidence about those stimuli, not a guarantee that a parameter separates all 32 species or that four controls suffice.

references.authors: Elhilali, Ma, Micheyl, Oxenham and Shamma
references.title: Temporal Coherence in the Perceptual Organization and Cortical Representation of Auditory Scenes
references.evidence: Human perceptual results showed that synchronous distant spectral components could group together even when the comparable successive components separated. The authors compared behavioural and ferret neural results and proposed a temporal-coherence model.
references.design_inference: If independent species need to remain audible, test separate phrase accents, gaps and contour timing alongside register and timbre; identical quantized pulses may fuse. Use synchrony deliberately when a blended ensemble is wanted.
references.limit: The experiment does not prescribe arbitrary event-time changes or prove reliable identification in a dense animal arrangement.

references.authors: Fischer, Soden, Thoret, Montrey and McAdams
references.title: Instrument Timbre Enhances Perceptual Segregation in Orchestral Music
references.evidence: Three orchestral-excerpt experiments found greater segregation with timbral heterogeneity, and lower segregation after reducing timbral differences. Ratings of isolated-stream blend did not predict global segregation; several musical/acoustic cues contributed.
references.design_inference: Judge presets in actual event arrangements as well as in isolation. Test phrase overlap, crossings and simultaneous attacks; a pleasant isolated voice may still disappear in context.
references.limit: The work used one/two-stream orchestral excerpts. It does not establish a maximum number of identifiable species or guarantee that more contrast always sounds better.

references.title: Magnitude Estimation of Conceptual Data Dimensions for Use in Sonification
references.evidence: Three experiments examined listeners’ scaling/polarity expectations for conceptual variables and auditory mappings, then tested matching auditory graphs to data. Appropriate mapping direction and amount depended on the concept.
references.design_inference: Validate actual data mappings separately from artistic species timbre. Do not assume that louder means more certain, higher means further north, or a faster phrase means an individual moved faster. Label the chosen mapping and preserve source uncertainty.
references.limit: This supports testing mappings; it does not validate the specific metaphor proposals in this bank.

references.title: Taxonomy and definitions for sonification and auditory display
references.evidence: This methodological paper distinguishes approaches such as direct parameter mapping and model-based sonification, and discusses the relationship of information-bearing sound and artistic uses.
references.design_inference: Keep traceable data relationships distinct from musical arrangement choices and source-inspired metaphors. A white-shark location can trigger an expressly artistic sound without being presented as an animal vocalization.
references.limit: A proposed taxonomy is a design framework, not a perceptual validation or an implementation benchmark.

evaluation_proposal: First compare near-neighbour species within a family at matched pitch, duration and perceived loudness; report distinctiveness separately from liking.
Then transpose each candidate across intended host registers and compare short/long contexts; preserve a recognisable body while retaining meaningful context differences.

Test the same captured events in sparse and dense mixes with fixed event provenance. Compare voice-only, phrases, phrase overlap and region processing; never claim isolated ratings predict ensemble clarity.
Use small balanced sessions with randomized order, repeats and an explicit unsure response. Measure confusion/ratings rather than forcing species recognition from untrained listeners.
Do not impose numeric pass thresholds or a voice-count ceiling from these papers. Define practical acceptance criteria with the owner and record audition decisions.
